preconditions.expression: all(1 <= n <= 3 * 10**5 and 0 <= m <= 3 * 10**5 for n, m in [line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[0:1]])
preconditions.description: The first line contains integers n (number of vertices) and m (number of edges) satisfying 1 ≤ n ≤ 3·10^5 and 0 ≤ m ≤ 3·10^5.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == 3 and all(int(x) for x in line.split()) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:1+m])
preconditions.description: Each of the next m lines contains three integers u_i, v_i, w_i (1 ≤ u_i, v_i ≤ n, u_i ≠ v_i, 1 ≤ w_i ≤ 10^9) representing an edge.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n for u in [int(stdin.splitlines()[-1])])
preconditions.description: The last line contains an integer u (1 ≤ u ≤ n) representing the start vertex.

preconditions.expression: len(set().union(*[{(int(x), int(y)) for x, y in [line.split()[0:2]]} for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:1+m]])) == m
preconditions.description: The graph has no multiple edges between the same pair of vertices.
The input has exactly m + 2 lines (1 for n and m, m for edges, 1 for u).

postconditions.expression: stdout.splitlines()[0].strip() == str(min_total_weight) and min_total_weight == sum(edge_weights[edge_idx - 1] for edge_idx in map(int, stdout.splitlines()[1].split()))
postconditions.description: The first line of stdout is the minimum total weight of the edges in the shortest-path tree, and the second line lists the indices of edges (1-based) included in the tree, such that their total weight equals the first line.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= edge_idx <= m for edge_idx in map(int, stdout.splitlines()[1].split()))
postconditions.description: All edge indices in the second line are valid (1 ≤ edge_idx ≤ m).
The edge indices in the second line are unique (no duplicates).

postconditions.expression: all(edge_idx in edge_indices for edge_idx in map(int, stdout.splitlines()[1].split()))
postconditions.description: The edge indices in the second line are a subset of the input edge indices (1-based).
The selected edges form a shortest-path tree from vertex u, where the shortest-path distances from u to all other vertices in the tree match those in the original graph.
